title: AI is giving everyone the same advice
lede: Cody Collier asked 65 AI models the same everyday questions ten times each and found their advice converges on a handful of default answers, set during fine-tuning.

points: Asked for a life-changing book, models named Man's Search for Meaning 73 times in 100; 98% said to put $10,000 in an index fund.
Variety appears only within one chat: new chats return the same first answer.
Invented people are 34 years old 69% of the time, and each lab has a signature name, such as Marisol for Claude and Elena for Gemini.
Answers to harmless questions identify a model's maker: 59% sit nearest a sibling from the same lab.
Measuring OLMo at each training stage, the favourite answer appears at supervised fine-tuning, not pretraining.

points.text: Some argue a generic question with no context should get the most likely answer, and much of this is sound consensus advice.
Others connect it to known research that RL training amplifies small preferences, visible in near-identical outputs across models.
One user got different answers with personalization on; a reply says a handful of tries proves little.
